title: Whistling Woods International Students Present 'Unbound' Collection at Bombay Times Fashion Week
summary: Student designers from Whistling Woods International's School of Fashion & Costume Design showcased 'Unbound', blending couture with kinetic engineering, at Bombay Times Fashion Week.
body_html:
Mumbai, 2 November 2026: Student designers from Whistling Woods International's (WWI) School of Fashion & Costume Design took centre stage at Bombay Times Fashion Week with 'Unbound', a runway showcase exploring the future of fashion. Around 48 student designers presented work that brought together wearable couture, kinetic mechanics and engineering.

Conceived as a challenge to traditional tailoring, 'Unbound' explores the meeting point of cultural heritage, kinetic technology, mythology and abstract art. Drawing on extensive original research, the students took inspiration from classical temple rituals, Mumbai's Art Deco architecture, and the raw aesthetics of motorsport, industrial metal and auto-rickshaw subcultures.

To take wearable art beyond conventional fabrics, the institute partnered with Thakur College of Engineering and Technology (TCET) as technology partner for the collection. The cross-disciplinary collaboration brought engineering into garment construction through dynamic rotating panels, kinetic mechanisms, integrated LED lighting, 3D printing and non-textile materials.

Actor and filmmaker Shreyas Talpade walked the ramp as the collection's showstopper, reflecting the students' innovative spirit and attention to structural craftsmanship. The presentation concluded with WWI leaders joining the runway, including Founder & Chairman Subhash Ghai, President Meghna Ghai Puri, Director of Academics Rahul Puri, and Head of the School of Fashion & Costume Design Jewellyn Alvares.

Appreciating the students' creativity and dedication, Meghna Ghai Puri, President of Whistling Woods International, said, “It is wonderful to see our students bring Unbound to a platform like Bombay Times Fashion Week. At Whistling Woods International, we encourage our students to experiment, think beyond conventions, and develop their own creative voices. Opportunities like these allow them to take their learning beyond the classroom, gain industry exposure, and grow in confidence as they prepare for their professional journeys. We are proud to see them push boundaries and bring their ideas to life.”

According to the institute, the fashion programme combines graded runway showcases, practical internships and masterclasses with industry experts, along with work in garment-construction labs, textile studios and digital fabrication facilities. The 'Unbound' showcase gave students the chance to present that learning on a professional runway before an industry audience.
